title: Analytics Queries in SQL
summary: Answer real business questions against an e-commerce database: aggregates, joins, anti-joins and window functions.

ShapeMismatch.hint: Your result has the wrong columns. Alias every output column exactly as the task specifies, e.g. SUM(...) AS revenue.

hints.test_revenue_by_category: Join order_items → orders → products, keep only status = 'completed', then GROUP BY category and ORDER BY revenue DESC. Wrap the sum in ROUND(..., 2).
hints.test_top_customers: Aggregate completed orders per customer: SUM(quantity * unit_price) and COUNT(DISTINCT order_id). ORDER BY total_spent DESC, customer_id, then LIMIT 5.
hints.test_monthly_revenue: substr(order_date, 1, 7) gives 'YYYY-MM'. Count DISTINCT orders, because joining to order_items repeats each order once per line.
hints.test_customers_without_orders: This is an anti-join: LEFT JOIN orders and keep rows where the order side IS NULL, or use NOT EXISTS.
hints.test_running_revenue: Compute monthly revenue in a CTE first, then SUM(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month) adds the running total.
hints.test_top_product_per_category: Rank products inside each category with ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY units DESC, product), then keep rank 1.
hints.test_queries_are_read_only: Each answer must be a single SELECT (or WITH … SELECT) statement, with no INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DROP and no extra statements after a semicolon.
